# AMLO 2022 — Chapter 5B Document Map (BOOK-013 / CIDOB biography) — Verified Draft

Coverage window in extract: 2007–6 August 2018, per the explicit "(Cobertura informativa hasta 6/8/2018)" cap in block 66. Source role: independent_reference (CIDOB biography, blocks 39–67).

## Source-level notes
- Document type: biography (chronological narrative).
- Institutional role: CIDOB research centre, Barcelona; the biography covers global and Mexican political dynamics (block 67).
- Coverage cap stated explicitly: "(Cobertura informativa hasta 6/8/2018)" — block 66. Nothing about the 2018–2024 AMLO presidency is covered here.
- The extract mixes observed facts (dates, vote shares, statutes), author framing ("tsunami", "colapso del PRI"), and subject self-report ("no mentir, no robar y no traicionar al pueblo"). Mark self-report as **subject assertion / campaign speech**, not evaluated outcome.

## Atomic claims with locators (5B-relevant)

### Track record & claims relevant to 5B.10, 5B.1, 5B.3
- **Block 48** — 2012 pledges: "incluyente" growth of 6% per year (described as triple the 12-year PAN average); 1.2 million jobs/year; minimum wage above inflation; popular housing; universal coverage in education and health, and pensions for adults 68+ and persons with disabilities. → **Campaign pledge; outcome not in extract.**
- **Block 62** — 2018 "austeridad republicana": no new taxes (some cuts in US-border states), no new debt; minimum wage raised gradually to 171 pesos by end of sexenio; pensions 1,500 pesos/month; energy/food self-sufficiency via local guarantee prices; Peña Nieto's energy reform to be reviewed and reversed where needed. → **Program commitment; execution not documented here.**
- **Block 63** — Platform 2018-2024: pragmatic social democracy; accepts "principios ortodoxos del libre mercado, el libre comercio, la estabilidad macroeconómica, la disciplina presupuestaria, la flotación del peso y la autonomía del Banco de México"; rejects "neoliberalismo", "tendencias privatizadoras", and "extranjerización" of strategic sectors. → **Author description of platform**, not outcome evaluation.

### Reform & appointment framing — 5B.2
- **Block 49** — Hypothetical 2012 cabinet: Cárdenas → Pemex; Ebrard → Gobernación; Poniatowska → Cultura. **Counter-factual / never materialised.**
- **Block 53** — MORENA officers Nov 2012: Martí Batres Guadarrama (CEN president), Bertha Elena Luján Uranga (secretaria general); López Obrador as Consejo Nacional president.
- **Block 56** — Nov 2015 (II Congreso Nacional): Polevnsky → secretaria general; Luján → Consejo Nacional; AMLO → CEN president by "aclamación", succeeding Batres.
- **Block 66** — 2018 majorities: Juntos Haremos Historia (MORENA + PT + PES) 308/500 deputies and 69/128 senators.
- **Block 63** — AMLO campaign statement: "No voy a meter a Peña Nieto en la cárcel" → **campaign pledge / self-restraint**.

### Crises, sanctions, inflation — 5B.9
- **Block 58** — EPN-era inflation cited as political pressure on incumbents; fuel and electricity price rises despite the 2013 energy reform supposedly being intended to lower prices. → **Author summary of pre-2018 conditions.**
- **Block 58–59** — Trump-era pressures on Mexico: wall, US tariffs on Mexican metals, renegotiation of NAFTA; AMLO position was to postpone NAFTA talks until after the 2018 election, vs. Peña Nieto's rush to close. → **Author description of pre-election positioning.**

### Energy, infrastructure, sectoral — 5B.6
- **Block 40–41** — 2008 energy-reform fight; PRD lost; Comisión Nacional de Hidrocarburos established; package approved October 2008 with PRI/PAN/PVEM plus "Los Chuchos" PRD votes.
- **Block 54** — EPN 2013 energy reform: ends Pemex/CFE monopoly regimes in practice ("en la práctica perdían sus regímenes de monopolio"); AMLO framed it as privatising "el legado del presidente Lázaro Cárdenas"; PRI counter-claim that state ownership of oil and gas was preserved. → **Contested claim from opposing camps.**
- **Block 64** — 2018 plan to scrap NAIM, instead develop Santa Lucía (AISL) on existing military facilities; cited "exorbitantes sobrecostes" and environmental impact as justifications. → **Author rationale for a still-unexecuted policy as of the extract.**

### Anti-corruption & rule of law — 5B.5, 5B.7
- **Block 46** — 2012 platform: "limpiar al Gobierno como a las escaleras, de arriba abajo"; anti-corruption bodies; truth commissions for FOBAPROA and Pemex; "no persecución contra nadie".
- **Blocks 63–64** — 2018 platform: revocation of mandate; desafuero for officials processed for corruption; "erradicar" corruption "dando ejemplo" from Los Pinos.
- **Block 65** — Victory-night speech: "Bajo ninguna circunstancia, el próximo presidente permitirá la corrupción ni la impunidad. Sobre aviso no hay engaño: sea quien sea, será castigado. Incluyo a compañeros de lucha, funcionarios, amigos y familiares." → **Campaign pledge, not evaluated outcome.**

### Distributional content — 5B.8
- **Block 48** — 2012 pledges: popular housing; universal education/health coverage; targeted pensions for adults 68+ and persons with disabilities.
- **Block 64** — 2018: free Internet nationwide; closing gender gaps, especially in labour; Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro scholarships; older-adult pensions. → **Pledges; no execution data in extract.**
- **Block 65** — "Por el bien de todos, primero los pobres" — **rhetorical framing**, not measured result.

### Other biographical / contextual notes
- **Block 54** — AMLO December 2013 "infarto agudo de miocardio" requiring surgery → biographical, not 5B-economic.
- **Block 58** — "200.000 personas habían sido asesinadas ya y varias miles más se encontraban desaparecidas o desplazadas" since 2006; author calls this "escalofriante estadística propia de un país en guerra civil" (no methodology shown here).
- **Block 65** — Author terms AMLO's victory "histórica" and (in block 66) "comparable a un tsunami"; PRI's defeat is "calificable de colapso." → **Author framing.**

## Limitations (must surface to next stage)
- Extract stops at 6/8/2018; **no 2022 policy execution, growth, inflation, debt, or distributional outcome data is present**. Treat any 5B answers leaning on this source for 2018–2022 as **unsupported** and refer to other dossier sources.
- Electoral returns are precisely stated (53.19% AMLO, 22.27% Anaya, 16.40% Meade, 5.23% Rodríguez Calderón); turnout 64.4% (block 65). Re-check against PREP/TEPJF originals before quoting.
- Power-sector and energy-reform framings reflect competing partisan narratives (López Obrador vs. EPN/PRI); the biography does not adjudicate — flag as **contested interpretation**, not adjudicated fact.
- Claims about Calderón-era crime tolls, "guerra civil" framing, and "200,000 asesinados" need corroboration from UCDP/INEGI elsewhere.

## Sections a stronger model should reopen
- 2012 cabinet counter-factual (block 49).
- Quantitative impact of Calderón drug war (block 58).
- 2013 energy reform legal content (block 54): constitutional articles amended, contract modalities opened — not detailed here.
- MORENA electoral arc 2015–2017 (blocks 55–57) for 5B.9 context on pre-2018 fiscal/macro environment.

**No 5B scoring attempted.**

## REOPEN REQUESTS
- Any 5B claim about 2018–2022 outcomes (growth, inflation, debt, distributional results, NAIM/AISL construction status, energy policy reversal, pension amounts, Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro scale, gender-labour reforms, Guardia Nacional deployment, anticorruption prosecutions including any desafuero action, revocation-of-mandate legislation, minimum-wage trajectory to 171 pesos, fuel/electricity price evolution). The extract provides only the pledges, not the execution; reopening any such claim here is not possible without a different dossier source.
- Quantitative methodology behind the "200,000 asesinados" since 2006 figure (block 58) — not stated in extract.
